findings.summary: The changelog guesses why decided proposals were on the 3 Nov page, and the real records and history contradict the guess. It then proposes an out-of-scope fix (a schedule trigger in pages.yml) that would not address the cause.
findings.evidence: Evidence snapshot: work-decisions 20261027-074524-5j98 approves ne91 (27 Oct), 20261030-081855-kh40 approves qyd9, and 20261030-081746-a1he decides jtd2 (30 Oct). history.json: 3b1f8c1 'Make the decisions page read approve/reject decisions from main' landed 2026-11-04T06:22. So the 3 Nov page was built by code that read decisions only from the records branch. It was not stale for lack of a push: decisions reach origin only by a push to main, and that push triggers pages.yml. The entry should name the records-branch-only read, fixed by the entry just below it, and drop the schedule-trigger proposal.
findings.location: CHANGELOG.md (new Fixed entry, 'Not fixed here' sentence)

findings.summary: The changelog gives ne91 as an example of a within-limit proposal 'nobody had to decide', but ne91 has an approval record.
findings.evidence: records/work-decisions/2026-10/20261027-074524-5j98.json has work_item 20261018-000648-ne91 with state approved. ne91 appeared on the page because that decision was not read, not because no limit was applied. The limit filter is still a valid fix, but this example misleads an outside reader about the cause.

summary: The code change is correct and small. render() now lists only open proposals above the raising role's limit, using may_change. A role with no recorded definition counts as above its limit. The empty state is one line, 'Nothing waiting for you', and the missing-branch message stays separate. The three new tests pass when I run `cargo test -p xtask decisions`, and the recorded fmt, clippy and test checks passed. Two problems fail the job. First, criterion 3 asks for a recorded run showing the locate() test failing on the old code. No such run is in the checks, and I cannot run the base here. Only the within-limit part of the test could fail on the base, because the base already drops decided proposals. The fixture also puts the rejection on the records branch, but reject-work commits to the current branch (main). Second, the CHANGELOG's account of why decided proposals were on the 3 Nov page is a guess, and the real records and history contradict it. All three named proposals were decided on main well before 3 Nov: ne91 approved on 27 Oct, qyd9 approved and jtd2 rejected on 30 Oct. The fix that made the page read decisions from main landed on 4 Nov (commit 3b1f8c1). So the 3 Nov page showed them because the code of that time did not read main's decisions, not because pages.yml left the page stale. The proposed schedule trigger would not have helped. The entry also gives ne91 as an example of a proposal 'nobody had to decide', but ne91 was approved.
